subject: Failover SLO and cost-split proposal for multi-region availability
messages:
From: Emma Zhao <emma@blueoak.com>
To: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-region availability + failover pricing question

Hi Chloe,

Quick intro: I'm Emma (VP of Platform Ops at BlueOak). We're evaluating Redwood for primary inference with a cross-region failover requirement (US + EU). Scope: production traffic ~100M inference tokens/month, occasional bursts to 3x baseline for seasonal events.

Questions we need answered to move to procurement:
- Do you price regional failover as an add-on or baked into an "Advanced" SLA?
- Can you split costs between our baseline committed capacity and burst (on-demand) so the burst doesn't skew our list price?
- What's the escalation coverage during EU nights (we need handoff + on-call 24/7 for critical incidents)?

I've attached a short requirements doc. Can you share a concise option set (pricing multipliers or % uplift), and any suggested commit term that gets us a better blended rate? We have a Q2 start window for a pilot.

Thanks — happy to take a short call if helpful.

--
Emma Zhao
VP, Platform Ops | BlueOak
emma@blueoak.com
4c4 Attachment: blueoak_requirements.pdf (1 page)

From: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Zhao <emma@blueoak.com>
Cc: Carlos Ruiz <carlos@blueoak.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-region availability + failover pricing question

Hi Emma,

Thanks for the clear brief and the requirements doc — helpful. High level, we typically offer three guardrails for availability/coverage; I'll map them to your asks below and include suggested commit levers:

1) Foundational (99.9%): baseline pricing (1.0x). SLO window: business-hours (M-F 8am-6pm local). No regional failover included; behaviour is routed to the closest healthy region.

2) Advanced Availability (99.95%): typical choice for cross-region setups (1.6x baseline). Includes active regional failover, priority routing, and a 4-hour P1 response target with 24/7 paging for on-call engineers. Burst capacity billed as on-demand at consumption rates unless you commit to a burst pool.

3) Enterprise Critical (99.99%): full NOC coverage, runbook integration, dedicated on-call rotation & quarterly on-site run-throughs (3.5x baseline). Best when outages are high-cost for the business.

Options to control blended cost for bursts:
- Commit model: purchase a reserved burst pool at a discounted rate (we price reserved burst at ~0.6x on-demand).
- Hybrid split billing: baseline covered under committed rate, bursts invoiced monthly at on-demand. We can cap monthly burst markup if you prefer a predictable ceiling.

Proposed next steps:
- If you want, I can run a quick SLO-cost model with your token distribution to show blended monthly spend across the models (I can share an xlsx).
- Suggest a 3-month pilot on Advanced (1.6x) with an option to convert to a 12-month commit with a 1.4x blended multiplier if committed within the pilot window.

Would you like me to send a short offer doc and the cost model? Happy to jump on a 30-min call this week.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.ai
4c4 Attachment: (can produce SLO_pricing_model_q1.xlsx on request)

From: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: FW: BlueOak SLO pricing — suggested concessions

Folks, forwarding BlueOak thread. Key asks: multi-region failover, controlled burst billing, 24/7 escalation for EU timezone. Pilot Q2.

My suggested play: offer Advanced at 1.6x for pilot (3 months) + one-time onboarding credit equal to 20% of first-month charges to remove friction. If they convert to 12-month commit within pilot, move them to 1.4x blended (reserve + burst pool).

Trade-offs to consider:
- If we discount Advanced below 1.5x, margin gets tight unless they take a burst reserve (we should require >=2x baseline reserve for the long term).
- Offer regional failover as included for Advanced but limit failover failback SLA to avoid unlimited cross-region egress costs; propose egress cap policy.

Attachments: SLO_pricing_model_q1.xlsx (spreadsheet with blended examples).

Ask: Marcus, can you validate the egress cap numbers (EU failover egress estimates) and confirm 1.4x is achievable with a 12-month commit at projected volumes? Priyom, please draft the offer doc and include the onboarding credit clause and egress cap language.

Thanks,
Chloe

From: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Zhao <emma@blueoak.com>, BlueOak Procurement <procurement@blueoak.com>
Cc: Carlos Ruiz <carlos@blueoak.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: BlueOak — proposed failover SLO offer and next steps

Hi Emma / Carlos,

Thanks for the sync earlier. Per our conversation, attached is a concise offer and the pricing breakdown. Highlights:

- Pilot: Advanced Availability (99.95%)
  - Length: 3 months
  - Pilot multiplier: 1.6x baseline
  - Onboarding: one-time credit equal to 20% of month-1 charges
  - Includes: active regional failover (US / EU), priority routing, 4-hour P1 target, 24/7 paging for critical incidents

- Path to commit (conversion option within pilot)
  - 12-month commit converts to blended multiplier of 1.4x (reserved baseline + reserved burst pool at discount).
  - Egress cap: monthly cross-region egress above forecasted baseline will be billed at on-demand but capped at 150% of forecasted monthly egress unless we mutually agree to expand the cap.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm you'd like the pilot to start on April 1.
2) If yes, we'll issue the pilot SOW and a DocuSign (attached is a draft).
3) Book a 30-min kickoff to align runbooks and alerting handoffs.

Attachments: BlueOak_Support_Offer_20270314.pdf, SLO_pricing_breakdown.csv

If the egress cap is a blocker, we can change to a tiered cap model — let me know. Happy to hop on a call to walk through line items.

Best regards,
